records.deidentified_narrative: at the listed date and time police responded to the above location for a report of a major vehicle crash in which a pedestrian was involved. u1 driver stated that she was driving nb on n walters and was turning wb on dignowity. u1 driver stated she did not see any cars coming and was then struck by u2 at the intersection. u1 driver advised she never saw the pedestrian (u3). u2 driver stated that he was traveling sb on n walters and there was a car stopped to turn eb [roadway]. as u2 approached the walters and dignowity intersection u1 turned in front of him causing the vehicles to collide. u2 driver stated that he never saw u3 until after the crash had already occurred. the front seat passenger also advised he never saw u3 and the back seat passenger said he was on his phone at the time of crash and didn't see anything. u3 appeared to be on the sidewalk at the time of the crash and was struck by u1 as a result of u2 striking u1. sgt r. cavazos #3374 was notified and on scene. tid det: b. martinez #2477 made scene and spoke with all parties involved. medical examiner's office was notified me: jerry leyva #105 me: [case id]. there were no signs of intoxicants by any of the drivers involved in the crash. this crash report was supplemented on [date] by tid det. b. martinez #2477 to add the results of the autopsy toxicology report, which indicated [person] was positive for cocaine at a level of 1. 6 mg/l.

records.deidentified_narrative: unit # 1 was traveling westbound in the [roadway]. the pedestrian was walking northbound on [roadway] in the [roadway]. unit # 1 approached the intersection of barnes and pace and advised that they did not see the pedestrian or dog in the intersection. driver of unit # 1 advised that she believed that she had struck the dog in the intersection and came to an immediate stop. driver of unit # 1 stated that she exited the vehicle and saw the pedestrian laying on the ground and went to render aid. a witness at the location arrived just seconds after the incident and also went to render aid. the witness advised that the pedestrian was laying in the same spot on the southeast corner of the intersection and had not moved. the witness advised that the pedestrian never lost consciousness the entire time she was on scene [medical facility] who advised that he had been struck by the vehicle and fell down. the pedestrian advised that he had lost consciousness several times at the scene and was having a hard time remembering what happened. officers at the scene inspected unit # 1 for damage and did not locate any damage on the vehicle. it did not appear that any of the dirt or dust on the vehicle had been disturbed. officer did locate a few dog hairs that were attached to the front left of the bumper, but the hairs were not stuck into the bumper. officer believe the dog was struck by the vehicle. it is the officer's opinion that when the dog was struck by the vehicle, the pedestrian attempted to pull the leash back and began to stumble and fell backwards on the roadway striking the back of his head. it is also possible that unit # 1 struck the dog and the dog hit the pedestrian knocking him backwards. officers do not believe that the unit # 1 ever actually struck the pedestrian. the pedestrian did not have any of injuries other than the back of his head that would be consistent with being struck by the vehicle.

records.public_safe_text: introduction:on [date] at approximately 1552 hours, i officer j. sloan 4205 with the surfside beach police department was headed to patrol the beach when i pulled up to a golfcart vs pedi accident. the accident was at the 100 block of beachfront. i was told by the mother who was idenified as [person] dob [date], dl 37574729 holding the injured child that she was hit by a golfcart. after looking at the child injuies i then call bcso to get medic 60 enroute to the location of the accident. the child was breathing,crying and had injuries on the top of her forehead with swelling. tran had remained holding child until the medic 60 pulled uptran had stated that ""i was holding my son and i turned around my daughter was hit over once and i yelled at the driver but they continue to drove the car and so my daughter got ran over twice , they stopped afterward"" i then checked on the driver of the golfcart that idenified himself as brandon falconer dob [date] txdl 45915862. falconer stated "" i was driving from the entrance of seaside. i was crusing down the beach. a little girl running across the sand quick. the parents just was watching her. i didnt see her at [roadway] and hit her with the golf cart ""around 1556 medic 60 rolled up to the scene to check on the well being of the small child. child was moved to the ambulance by stetcher by christina edwards (in charge) and was in full care of childs furter treatment. minutes after ems evaluated the child a call for life flight was called in by medics to freeport. i walked over to the passenger of the golf cart was idenified as hannah simyers dob [date]. simyers stated "" i was driving and we switched drivers right before it happened. i was in the passenger and the little girl ran out in front of us. we were going slow under the speed limit "" medic 60 left the sand to head towards 10 surf to the landing zone of life flight to pick up child. i headed to the landing zone myself to the scene and meet medic 60 on scene . after 10 minutes life flight then landed on the ground to take care over on child . child then was moved by stretcher onto chopper where was lifted off the ground heading towards [medical facility] [medical facility] in houston texas. details: statements of all parties along with pictures were taken at scene and report was taken. all parties were released and no further information at this time.

provided in call slip. witness phone # 504-502-6940thursday, april 7, 2022=====akinade adesina - adesina responded to the pd to be interviewed. this interview was recorded and a copy of the interview was placed into the 2022 digitial recording file folder. during this interview adesina advised that he initially observed zion standing near a pole on the sidewalk monitoring his cellphone. adesina advised that he was stopped behind the stop line as he observed zion. adesina stated that he received a green light to proceed through the intersection and noticed that pedestrians had a ""hand sign"" or do not cross. adesina stated that as he proceed through the intersection he could only recall seeing zion dart in front of his vehicle. adesina advised that he immediately applied the brakes to stop his vehicle. he advised that he immediately stopped to check the welfare of zion who advised that he was okay. adesina stated that after ensuring that zion was okay, he proceeded to leave the scene. he advised when he last observed zion he was upright and walking. i photographed adesina's vehicle and placed these photos in the 2022 incoming evidence photos folder. natasha wiley 903. 239. 3404 - i spoke with wiley and provided her adesina's insurance information. as well, i informed wiley that i would need zion's medical records. michael kelly 504. 502. 6940 - i attempted to contact kelly but was forced to leave a voice mail message for a return call. it should be noted on the date of the crash, adesina's vehicle bore tx lp 1bg1295 which returned to taiwo otuya reboboth enterprise [roadway], huntsville, tx. on this date, [date], adesina's vehicle now displayed tx lp [identifier] which returns to, akinade adesina, [roadway] #227, huntsville, tx. monday, april 11, 2022=====natasha wiley 903. 239. 3404 - i spoke with wiley and provided her adesina's name and information as the driver of the vehicle that struck zion. as well, i asked wiley to have zion contact me so that he could be interviewed. i also asked wiley to have zion bring his medial records. tuesday, april 12, 2022=====michael kelly 504. 502. 6940/kellymichaelmk@yahoo. com - i attempted to contact kelly but was forced to leave a voice mail message for a return call (x2). i have also emailed kelly and asked him to contact me. zion alex 903. 746. 7377 - i spoke with zion on this date. zion advised that he would respond to the pd tomorrow to be interviewed. as well, i asked zion to bring what medical records he may have access to at the moment. while reviewing officer hill's body camera, wiley stated that he was ""okay"" upon officer hill introducing himself. when asked how hard he was hit, zion stated not very hard. he further stated that adesina did exit his vehicle to check if he was okay. wednesday, april 13, 2022=====zion alex - alex responded to the pd to be interviewed on this date. this interview was recorded by the interview room cameras. alex [roadway] [roadway]. he stated he observed a [roadway] j to [roadway]. alex initially stated that he didn't see traffic light, but he had walk signal. alex then stated that he believed the traffic light was green but not to certain. alex stated driver side struck him on left side of his body, hard enough to knock him off his feet onto the roadway. he was able to catch himself on all fours, and ""wasn't hurt too badly."" alex stated he was able to get up and was asked by the vehicle operator if he, alex, was okay. he gave a thumbs up and got out [roadway]. alex stated he did not ask for any information, but was more concerned about getting out of the roadway. he stated other passers by were able to obtain the license plate of the vehicle that left. he advised he got a ride to the gas station. alex stated he had no broken bones but was sore on left side a few days after the crash. after seeing medical attention he learned he had a concussion. i asked alex if he felt he needed and ambulance or after contacting his mother, he was directed to contact ems. alex advised that he felt okay, but his mother advised him that he could have internal injuries that he could not see and to contact ems. alex also informed me that the crash report drawing was incorrect. i have since corrected this report. michael kelley 903. 746. 7377 - i spoke with kelly on this date. kelley advised that he did not witness the crash but advised he assisted zion getting up off the ground. he advised that he did observe the other driver leave the scene. kelley provided a ride to the gas station where zion was met by ems. i have included a partial recording of this conversation with kelly. when moving the file i ""cut"" the file, then deleted it from my voice recording folder. when i attempted to paste the file, i received and error message. tuesday, april 26, 2022=====zion alex 903. 746. 7377 - i spoke with zion on this date. zion advised that he has returned home, and got preoccupied. he advised that he would deliver the medical records as soon as he could.

regarding a child being struck by a vehicle and the driver leaving. upon my arrival, i met with shaniqua in the parking lot of the north station to gather information about the incident. she stated [roadway] [school facility], located at [roadway], around 1550 hours. while driving southwest bound in the [roadway], she stated a young black male (jamar) entered the roadway. shaniqua said it looked like he was trying to pick something up, but she hit him with the front bumper on the passenger side. she stressed she could not stop immediately due to the vehicles behind her, [roadway] and pulled over to the first available, which we [roadway], and then ran back towards the area where jamar was struck. she headed back and saw some children walking away, so she began yelling at them, trying to locate jamar. shaniqua stated the kids would end up stopping and told her jamar was picked up by a random person (erica) who took him home. when she asked about his injuries, they commented jamar was complaining about his foot being injured. thus, due to jamar leaving the area, [school facility] to pick up her children from the main office. she had called her older daughter at 1354 to instruct her to wait at the office because a child was hit; i saw the call log. after picking up her children, she immediately came to the main station to make the report. based on this conversation, it appears that shaniqua had stopped immediately once it was safe for her to do so to comply with the duty to give information and render aid. officer burton and i then headed [medical facility], officer burton spoke to jamar while i talked to his mother, kendra, who stated erica had taken jamar to her residence. still, [school facility] to pick up jamar because her daughter called to make her aware that jamar was hit. after speaking with both individuals, we found that jamar did not suffer any severe injuries, and he told burton he had [roadway] southbound to another side where his sister was. once he reached that side, he ran back and would get hit at this point. based on the information, unit 1 was traveling southwest bound in the [roadway] when jamar was struck. i activated my body-worn camera at the beginning of this call and used it to take photos of the damage to the vehicle. end of report. beat 220unit 0474

records.deidentified_narrative: i was dispatched [roadway] and elm park for a motor vehicle vs. pedestrian accident. i arrived on location and contacted the pedestrian (unit 2) and asked if he needed medical attention. unit 2 stated he did not want ems but, advised me he had some small, superficial scrapes on his forearms. unit 2 stated he was riding his long [roadway] [roadway] stop intersection of elm park. unit 2 stated as he was riding down the hill he observed unit 1 drive through the intersection going nw bound on elm park and unit 2 couldn't stop due to his long board not having brakes. unit 2 stated he struck the ""tail end"" of unit 1 but, jumped off his long board in time so he wouldn't be stuck under unit 1. unit 2 stated he flew through the air and slid into the grass of a nearby residence and only suffered superficial injuries but, wasn't sure how he would feel the next day. unit 2 was offered ems multiple times but, declined the service. i next spoke with the driver of unit 1 (driver 1). driver 1 stated neither her nor her passengers had injuries. the driver stated she didn't disregard the stop sign and observed unit 2 run over a large branch in the roadway which caused him to fly off the long board. unit 1 stated unit 2 was changing his story from what he told her earlier regarding how he lost control on the long board and what unit 2 was saying wasn't what happened. driver 1 stated unit 2 initially took responsibility for losing control on his own but, started voicing a complaint about his long board being damaged and wanted compensation. driver 1 stated she then called for police. driver 1 allowed me to examine her vehicle and i could not observe any dents on her vehicle where anything could have impacted it. i also didn't see any smears, hand prints, disturbances in the layer of dirt/dust or anything that indicated an impact occurred with unit 1. i spoke with unit 2 again and he stated he had ridden his long board past the stop sign without stopping and collided with the front passenger side of unit 1. i found this to be inconsistent with what was told to me earlier but, unit 2 appeared to be very upset at the ordeal and believed he could have been seriously hurt or killed. no witnesses were on scene to observe the collision or lack thereof. i did not observe the crash occur in my presence or view and my opinion is based on the information provided to me by those involved and my own observations. driver 1 and unit 2 both advised me they wished to solve the matter amongst themselves without involving insurance but, due to the circumstances i found it appropriate to investigate the incident and write a report. based on what i observed and what i was advised, i believed it was possible unit 2 had ridden his long board into an obstruction in the roadway which caused him to lose control. it is also possible unit 2 may have collided with unit 1 in the listed areas but, i did not observe any visible evidence of this occurring on unit 1. at this point, if there was a crash, i believe unit 2 didn't stop at the stop sign due to his high speed of travel and collided with unit 1. both parties were provided with the [case id] and each others information via sapd crash forms. no further action was taken. dme is available.

[case id] was given to v-1's roomate. no further actions were taken, coban/bwc available.
